turns: I have a two-year work permit in Sweden. What salary does my job need to pay?
question: And can my spouse come here and work too?
reference_answer: Yes, normally. The spouse or partner of someone with a work permit can be granted a residence permit under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen, if the person in Sweden can support themselves and the spouse (the level: salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, counting the spouse too, 4 kap. 4 c §; exceptions for special reasons). The permit is valid for the same period as the work permit. A person with a temporary residence permit may be given a work permit under 6 kap. 3 § utlänningslagen, unless reasons related to the purpose of the residence permit speak against it; Migrationsverket's page says adult family members are permitted to work.
notes: Multi-turn (phase 5): the permit type comes only from the earlier turn; plain RAG asks the question alone. Legal basis checked 2026-11-24: a work-permit holder's family is granted permits under 4 kap. 4 a § utlänningsförordningen (maintenance requirement, level in 4 c §, no housing-size requirement, same validity as the worker's permit), not 5 kap. 3 a § / 3 j § utlänningslagen. Same facts as family-spouse-004 (corrected 2026-11-24).

turns: I've had work permits in Sweden for four and a half years. Can I get permanent residence?
question: What else do I need besides the time?
reference_answer: Besides four years with a permit for work during the last seven (5 kap. 5 § utlänningslagen), permanent residence requires that the person can support themselves and that, given their expected conduct, there is no doubt it should be granted (5 kap. 7 §). The ordinance sets the support level: salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, counting only the person themself, with some permanence (4 kap. 4 e § utlänningsförordningen). Exceptions for special reasons are in 5 kap. 8 §.

turns: I'm in Sweden on a work permit, and my employer has just told me my job ends at the end of the month.
question: How long do I have, and does the time start now or when the job ends?
reference_answer: The permit may be revoked when the employment has ended, unless within three months the person gets a new job covered by the permit, or applies for a work permit for a new job and that application is later granted (7 kap. 3 § första stycket 2 utlänningslagen). It is a 'may', not an automatic expiry. Migrationsverket counts the three months from the last day of employment.

turns: My work permit was granted in February 2026.
question: I'm registering my extension application this week. What salary will I need?
reference_answer: Because the permit was granted before 1 June 2026 and the extension is registered with Migrationsverket by 1 December 2026, the older wording of 6 kap. 2 § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen applies (transitional provision 2 to SFS 2026:295; the same for the ordinance in SFS 2026:605): the employment must give good maintenance (god försörjning), which the ordinance (5 kap. 8 a § utlänningsförordningen in its older wording) defined as a salary of at least 80 percent of the median salary published by Statistics Sweden. The new requirement of at least 90 percent of the median salary does not apply to this extension. Salary, insurance and other terms must still be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice.

turns: I have a work permit tied to my current employer, and another company has offered me a job.
question: Do I apply for a new permit or an extension before I start there?
reference_answer: The law treats a new job during a valid permit as an extension: 6 kap. 4 a § utlänningslagen allows an extension if the new employment meets 2 § första stycket, and for a new employment also 2 § andra stycket. In Migrationsverket's e-service the application is made as an extension ("Extend the existing work permit") while the current permit is valid. Migrationsverket's page on changing employer calls this a new application: the permit is tied to an employer, so the new job needs a new decision, but the application category is the extension. An answer should lead with the extension and explain the page's wording, so the applicant chooses the right option.

turns: I'm here on a work permit, and my spouse has a family permit tied to mine but doesn't work.
question: When I get permanent residence, can my spouse get it too?
reference_answer: Not at the same time as such, and normally not without an income. Migrationsverket first decides the worker's permanent residence; the spouse's application is then examined. Once the worker has permanent residence, the spouse can be granted permanent residence when the permit expires if they have had a temporary permit for at least three years, the conditions for a family permit under 5 kap. 3 a § are met (tied to someone with permanent residence, which brings the worker's maintenance and housing requirement in 3 j §), and the special requirements of 5 kap. 7 § are met (5 kap. 3 m § fjärde stycket utlänningslagen). 7 § requires the spouse to be able to support themselves; the ordinance sets the level: salary after preliminary tax of at least the protected amount for wage garnishment, counting only the person themself, and unemployment benefits do not count (4 kap. 4 e § utlänningsförordningen). Exceptions for special reasons are in 5 kap. 8 §. If permanent residence is refused, Migrationsverket considers a temporary permit instead.
notes: Multi-turn (phase 5): the scored question only makes full sense with the earlier turn; plain RAG asks it alone. Same facts as family-spouse-put-income-401 (checked); that the spouse has no job is only in the earlier turn. 401's basis re-checked 2026-11-24: 5 kap. 3 m § fjärde stycket holds once the worker has permanent residence.
